data.cultural_impact: Atira is a Sanskrit name rooted in Hindu tradition and culture, it is often given to a baby girl as it represents the divine and radiant energies associated with the deities. This name is unique and reflects the rich heritage of Indian culture, offering a strong sense of identity and pride.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spiritualism, the name Atira holds deep meaning. It represents the shining light and power of the divine, symbolizing hope, joy, and enlightenment. It is believed that the name bestows blessings of prosperity, happiness, and spiritual growth upon the child, making it a cherished name among Hindus.

historical_references.reference: Atira was a queen consort of the Shakambhari Chalukya king, Vijayaditya Siddeshvara (1127-1158 CE). She is mentioned in the inscription on the Raktasagara Tank at Gadag, Karnataka.

Another reference to Atira can be found in the Prabandha Samudracharya of the 13th century Kannada poet, Sarangapani. In this work, Atira is described as the queen of the Vijayanagara king, Veera Ballala I (1234-1268 CE).
